brief.text:
This region covers Stencil's security and compliance program, centered on SOC 2 readiness and third-party vendor risk management. Sam Whitfield runs the program and Maya Chen is the executive approver. Ledgerwise Assurance issued an unqualified (clean) SOC 2 Type I report dated 2026-06-30 with two observations. The Type II observation window runs through the end of 2026, and fieldwork is scheduled for January 2027. The team decided not to ask Ledgerwise to shorten or restart the observation window. The status letter to Northfield will list the three known gaps plainly, without polish. Controls rated healthy include change management, offboarding, security training, backup restore testing and incident handling. One question is still open: whether the investing backend (`brokerd`) is in scope for Type II. Policy documents each have named owners. The strategy doc is reviewed and revised quarterly.

The Q3 access review covered 20 systems, each with a tier, owner, account count, removals or reductions, and a sign-off date. Fourteen of the 20 (70%) are signed off. Plaid, Lithic, PagerDuty, Snowflake, Customer.io and Branch are still pending. The review overran its Sep 21–30 window, so an exception must be documented, and the target completion date is 2026-10-10. As of 2026-10-11 that target has passed, so the remaining sign-offs should be treated as overdue. A separate low-severity open risk tracks a fix to fractional share position reconciliation.

Vendor risk policy requires that every vendor touching Confidential or Restricted data be assessed before contract. Contracts must include breach notification, data deletion on termination and audit rights. The vendor risk register flags concentration risk on Pillar Bank (the sponsor bank), Plaid and DriveWealth. It sets quarterly and annual review routines and lists Tier 3 operational vendors: GitHub, Sidekiq Pro, and Persona, which is being phased out. Open questions include a backup sponsor bank, MX as a backup for Plaid, and a DriveWealth alternative.

The DriveWealth security questionnaire found strong controls overall, with three issues. DriveWealth's 72-hour breach notification window conflicts with Stencil's 24-hour obligation to Pillar Bank. Its sandbox lacks corporate action simulation. Production credential access was reduced from 3 engineers to 2.

The Lithic assessment covers the debit card, which is tied to the Stencil balance and issued on a Pillar Bank BIN with virtual and physical cards, spend controls and layered fraud defenses. The Lithic sandbox uses only synthetic data. At launch, Restricted and Confidential cardholder data and tokens will be shared, but full card numbers never touch Stencil systems. Evidence reviewed includes a PCI DSS Level 1 AOC, a SOC 2 Type II report, a pen test summary, multi-region continuity with a 2-hour RTO, and a funding review. Pillar Bank's compliance review of the card program is not yet complete. The card soft launch moved to Q1 2027 to protect investing GA and the Series B. Pillar Bank conditions include a $2,500 daily funding cap per user for the first 90 days of investing.

Typical questions about this region: when SOC 2 Type II fieldwork happens, which access review systems are unsigned, why the Lithic launch slipped, how to resolve the DriveWealth notification SLA conflict, and which vendors are concentration risks.

items.title: Where are we on SOC 2 Type II readiness, and what gaps are left?
items.body:
## Where SOC 2 Type II stands

**Type I is done and clean.** Ledgerwise Assurance issued an unqualified (clean) SOC 2 Type I report on 2026-06-30, covering control design and implementation as of 2026-05-31 against the Security and Availability criteria, with 2 observations [c8][c6]. Those Type I observations have since been closed [c12]. The report is internal-only — external sharing requires an NDA and Maya Chen's approval [c8].

**The Type II observation window is open and runs 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31** [c8][c7]. Type I only proved controls were *designed* correctly at a point in time; Type II tests whether they *operated* across the whole window [c8]. Sam Whitfield owns the program, Maya Chen is executive approver [c1].

Scope: production AWS, the Rails monolith, Go money movement services, mobile backend APIs, CI/CD and tooling. Snowflake analytics and the marketing site are out of scope. AWS, Pillar Bank, Plaid, Alloy and DriveWealth are carved out as subservice organizations [c1][c8].

## The gaps

Sam's internal readiness review on 2026-09-10 — the midpoint of the window — walked every recurring control and asked whether evidence would survive a Ledgerwise sample. Most controls were healthy; **three gaps would produce Type II exceptions if not closed and documented** [c18]. Status below is as of the Oct 9 update, so it may be ~2 days stale against today:

| # | Gap | Severity | Owner | Due | Status (Oct 9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Q3 quarterly access review not done | High | Sam | 2026-10-10 | 70% (14 of 20 systems) |
| 2 | Vendor risk assessments missing for DriveWealth, Lithic, Alloy, Customer.io | Medium | Sam | 2026-10-24 | 2 of 4 done |
| 3 | MDM on 88% of laptops (60 of 68); control requires 100% | Medium | Sam | 2026-10-17 | 96% (65 of 68) |

**Gap 1 — access review (the one that already slipped).** The Access Review Procedure requires a quarterly review of every in-scope system by quarter end. Q3 hadn't started as of Sep 10, largely because Sam spent August on policies and system owners were deep in the ACH cut-over and investing beta. The Sep 21–30 rerun **missed Sep 30** [c18]. Six systems remain pending in the Q3 Access Review Tracker: Plaid dashboard and Lithic dashboard (both Tier 1, Marcus), PagerDuty and Snowflake (Tier 2), and Customer.io and Branch (Tier 3) [c22]. Note that two of the six are Tier 1 money-moving vendor portals, which is a harder story than "lower-risk tools." The late completion will be documented as an exception with root cause (launch load on owners), and **Q4's review starts Dec 1** rather than mid-December to avoid a repeat before the window closes [c18].

**Gap 2 — vendor risk assessments.** The Vendor Risk Register lists every critical vendor, but four had never been formally assessed against the questionnaire: DriveWealth (live since beta), Lithic (signed, not live), Alloy (KYC since June), Customer.io (marketing notifications). DriveWealth closed 2026-09-24 and Lithic 2026-10-02. **The two still open are Alloy — waiting on their current SOC 2 bridge letter — and Customer.io, whose questionnaire is with their team** [c18]. Both remaining items depend on an external party, so the Oct 24 due date isn't fully under Sam's control. This matters beyond the audit: policy requires every vendor touching Confidential or Restricted data to be assessed before contract and reviewed annually, with contracts carrying breach notification, data deletion on termination and audit rights [c11][c10].

**Gap 3 — MDM coverage.** 68 laptops total (62 employee macOS, 4 contractor macOS, 2 Linux engineering workstations). Enrollment went 11 (Jul 31) → 39 (Aug 21) → 60 (Sep 10) → 65 (Oct 8), i.e. 96% against a control requiring 100% [c20]. **Three remain**: two Linux workstations (macOS MDM can't manage them, so they get an endpoint agent plus a script-enforced baseline reported to the SSO posture check — one installed, second scheduled Oct 13) and one laptop belonging to someone on leave until Oct 14, enrollment booked for their first morning back and the device blocked from SSO meanwhile [c18][c20]. No exceptions were granted; a request to exempt a Linux workstation was declined. Phase 5 (posture check blocks SSO) doesn't start until 100% [c20].

## Other open threads

- **Investing scope is unconfirmed.** Sam still needs to confirm investing-product scope with Ledgerwise [c1][c14] — worth resolving early, since scoping the investing product in late would mean evidence for a period already partly elapsed.
- **Exceptions register unpublished.** Sam has an open action to publish it [c9] — relevant given Gap 1 will itself be documented as an exception.
- **Northfield diligence.** Maya owns sending the SOC 2 status letter and data room to Northfield [c1][c14], with a diligence call on Oct 14 [c12]. A DriveWealth API key compromise tabletop is also planned for Q4 [c12].

## Framing

The honest read: all three gaps are remediation-in-progress rather than unknowns, and two of three are near the line. But Type II tests operation *over the window*, so closing a gap in October doesn't erase the months it was open — Gap 1 in particular is already a certain exception, and the remediation plan is about documenting it well, not avoiding it. Closing these before the 2026-12-31 window ends was explicit enough as a Q4 priority that it was one of the reasons the Sep 30 review pushed the card soft launch from Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, alongside Investing GA, the Series B close, and the ADR-031/ADR-032 round-up follow-ups [c2][c24].

One caveat on sourcing: the status figures above all trace to the Oct 9 update on the readiness review and the Oct 8 MDM snapshot. Given today is Oct 11 and Gap 1's target was Oct 10, the access review may well have closed already — the map doesn't show anything more recent.
